title: Stray Kids’ ‘THIS & THAT’ Album: All 7 Tracks Ranked
summary: After eight years together, the group best known for maximalism makes a strong case for pulling back.
body: At this point in their careers, Stray Kids have turned topping the Billboard 200 into something of a tradition. Since signing with Republic Records in the U.S. in 2022, every one of the octet’s Korean albums — Oddinary , Maxident (both 2022), 5-Star , Rock-Star (both 2023), ATE , HOP (both 2024), KARMA and DO IT (both 2025) — has debuted at No. 1, making them the first act in the chart’s history to open on top with their first eight charted releases. Released via JYP Entertainment and the REPUBLIC Collective, THIS & THAT is out today (Aug. 7) to mark the group’s ninth swing to extend that historic streak in the States, while having a higher international profile than ever. After headlining Governors Ball in New York before a reported 45,000 people earlier this summer, Stray Kids are set to become the first international male act to hold their own concert at Tokyo’s Olympic-sized National Stadium later this month before headlining Brazil’s Rock in Rio in September, and launching their STRAYCITY festival series across North, South and Latin American countries. title: ‘The Industry At Large Benefits From Independent Thought & Experimentation’ Says Co-Founder of Dance Festival Elements
summary: The independent fest is happening this weekend in Long Pond, PA. Co-founder Brett Herman talks about Elements' growth and "infinite plan of upgrades."
body: The 2026 edition of Elements festival is getting underway today (Aug. 7) at Pocono Raceway in Long Pond, Pennsylvania. Having started in 2013 as a one-day event in Brooklyn, Elements has over the years transformed into a sprawling three-day fest in the Pocono Mountains, with the event itself largely taking place in the woods behind the racetrack. While Elements is and always has been an independent festival, it’s got a lineup to compete with any major dance gathering. This year’s bill includes Charlotte de Witte, Chris Lake, Subtronics, Porter Robinson, Of the Trees, Above & Beyond, Cloonee, Excision and Azzeca, with organizers expecting a crowd of up to 40,000, up from the 33,000 hosted in 2025. The event is produced by its co-founders Brett Herman and Timothy Monkiewicz along with a core team of 20 and many more during the festival itself. With its whimsical vibes, Elements draws comparisons to other North American dance festivals Lightning in a Bottle, Electric Forest and Shambhala, and draws many of the same attendees as well. In their own ways, all four events take inspiration from Burning Man, an event Herman has attended 20 times — and, with the team, has consciou…

title: Executive Turntable: SiriusXM Names Jenny Tartikoff Senior VP & Head of Communications
summary: This week's column features the launch of Andrew Kautz's Kautz & Associates, Allen Mitchell's Reverie Ranch Group & more music industry hires and promotions.
body: SiriusXM has named Jenny Tartikoff the company’s new senior vp and head of communications, effective on Monday, Aug. 10. She will report to Scott Greenstein , the company’s president and chief content officer. In her new role, Tartikoff will oversee SiriusXM’s content and serve as an advisor to its leadership team. Tartikoff joins SiriusXM from Paramount Pictures, where she served as executive vp of global communications. Prior to that, she was head of content and advertising communications at Spotify and had been senior vp of global communications at Universal Filmed Entertainment Group. At the beginning of her career, she worked in communication for broadcast journalism, working at NBC News. “Jenny is an accomplished communications leader with the judgment, range and industry experience to help SiriusXM tell a clear and compelling story, anchored around making SiriusXM the definitive home for audio content and fandom,” Greenstein said in a statement. “Jenny’s experience across entertainment, streaming, podcasting and advertising makes her the right leader to guide our communications into the next phase of SiriusXM’s strategy across our portfolio of audio businesses, and we…

title: Google Messages makes one-handed use much easier with new rollout
summary: The new, redesigned floating context menu and selective text copying make messaging on large phones less frustrating.
body: Credit: Sanuj Bhatia / Android Authority TL;DR Google Messages is expanding its server-side rollout of the floating context menu and selective text copying to more beta users. The redesigned floating menu places actions like Reply, Copy, Edit, Star, and Delete in a clean vertical list right by the text bubble for easier one-handed use. Selective text copying introduces draggable handles, allowing users to highlight specific details without copying an entire message. Google Messages finally appears to be expanding a major usability refresh to more users, bringing its redesigned floating context menu and selective text copying to (slightly) wider availability. Reddit user seeareeff reports that they could finally see the new floating context menu when long-pressing a message bubble. Rather than dumping action icons into the top action bar (which forced awkward hand re-gripping on larger phones), the vertical floating menu appears right below/above the text. Essential actions like Reply, Copy, Edit, Star, and Delete are neatly grouped in a clean list format that makes one-handed interaction far less frustrating.

title: The Galaxy Z Fold 8 is the wrong Samsung foldable to buy this year
summary: It's giving middle-child energy.
body: Samsung gave us two very different foldables this year: the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra . Both these foldables are aimed at completely different people. The Fold 8 introduces a new direction for Samsung with a wider display, a thinner chassis, and a much more compact feel in the hand. Meanwhile, the Fold 8 Ultra carries forward what the Galaxy Z Fold 7 started, refining that familiar formula. Here’s the thing, though: you’d expect two completely different form factors to come with equally different feature sets. Instead, they’re remarkably similar, and the Fold 8 Ultra is priced just $200 more than the Fold 8. That’s exactly what got me thinking. For such a relatively small price increase, the Ultra offers enough extra value that it almost feels like Samsung is nudging buyers in that direction.

title: The OnePlus 15 and 15R just got ColorOS beta
summary: The update, likely based on Android 17, is currently open to OnePlus 15 series in India.
body: TL;DR OnePlus has opened the first global ColorOS closed beta for the OnePlus 15 and 15R. The testing program is currently limited to Indian variants and excludes US, EU, and global models. OnePlus hasn’t confirmed the wider rollout yet. OnePlus has officially begun its transition from OxygenOS to ColorOS , opening the first global Closed Beta Testing (CBT) program for the OnePlus 15 and OnePlus 15R. If you’ve been wondering when the software migration announced alongside the company’s withdrawal from the US and European smartphone markets would actually begin, this is the clearest sign yet that it’s now underway. There’s one important catch, though. While both the OnePlus 15 and OnePlus 15R are available in the US, the inaugural ColorOS beta is currently reserved exclusively for Indian variants of the two phones. There’s no mention of the base OS, but Android 17 is expected, given that OnePlus has been testing the OS on the OnePlus 15 since March .

title: Samsung’s latest 200MP sensor could be a fantastic upgrade for Galaxy S27 Ultra
summary: This new sensor could be just what Samsung's flagships need in the wake of LOFIC-equipped camera sensors.
body: Credit: Stephen Radochia / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung has announced the ISOCELL HPC 200MP camera sensor for smartphones. This sensor brings a new pixel structure that enables dramatically improved dynamic range, reduced noise, and more. This would be a significant improvement over the 200MP sensor currently used on Samsung’s Ultra phones. Samsung debuted the first 200MP smartphone camera sensor back in 2022, and it has offered a variety of 200MP sensors since then. The pixels on these sensors are tiny, though, which isn’t great for image quality. However, the company’s latest 200MP camera sensor brings an interesting solution. Samsung has quietly announced the ISOCELL HPC camera sensor (thanks, Dylan H!). At first glance, this 200MP sensor has a lot in common with the ISOCELL HP2 used on the Galaxy S26 Ultra and its predecessors. That means a 1/1.3-inch sensor, 0.6-micron pixels, and Super Quad Phase-Detection autofocus.

title: August’s Android Canary release gets app handles and new Quick Settings layout editor
summary: Sadly, it's also the end of the line for Pixel 6 phones.
body: TL;DR Google’s latest Android Canary build is now out, supporting Pixel 6 and newer hardware. This will be the final Android Canary release for the Pixel 6 and Pixel 6 Pro. Today’s 2608 build introduces some new ways to customize Quick Settings. Google’s got tons of options right now for testers looking to get a taste of Android’s latest changes before anybody else, but you absolutely need to be first in line, there’s no better option than the Android Canary program. It’s been exactly one month since the 2607 July build arrived, and Google is now back with August’s Android Canary 2608. Over on Reddit’s Canary sub, Google shares the news of Android Canary 2608’s availability. Sadly, it’s not all good, and we’ve got some bad news for testers hoping to eke a little more life out of some of Google’s oldest hardware: Just like Android 17 QPR2 , Canary is also dropping support for the Pixel 6 and Pixel 6 Pro . The good news is that you can still install today’s release — but that’s it; you’re cut off, going forward.

title: GrapheneOS isn’t pulling any punches in its beef with Revolut
summary: The gloves are off as GrapheneOS calls Revolut's approach to security "incredibly negligent."
body: Credit: Calvin Wankhede / Android Authority TL;DR GrapheneOS says some users are once again having trouble logging into the Revolut app. The project claims Revolut is specifically targeting GrapheneOS while still supporting outdated Android versions. GrapheneOS suggests a possible workaround but warns that it may not continue to work in the long term. Banking apps can be suspicious of anything that strays from the standard Android experience, but GrapheneOS clearly believes Revolut is taking that distrust way too far. The privacy-focused Android project claims some users are once again having trouble logging into the Revolut app, accusing the fintech company of deliberately trying to shut them out. In a thread on X , GrapheneOS said Revolut is blaming the restriction on security concerns, but argued that the real issue is that they’re enforcing licensing on Google Play . It also questioned how strict Revolut’s security standards can really be when the app still supports Android 9, which launched back in 2018. It went further, describing Revolut as “incredibly negligent when it comes to security.”

title: Maybe the FCC was onto something: These routers are phoning home to China with a secret backdoor
summary: Of course, because they predate the ban, the FCC continues to permit their sale.
body: TL;DR A new report details a massive security flaw in Zbtlink-made routers. The routers are programmed to ping a hard-coded list of servers, traced back to China. Once connected, the routers grant full root access — no authentication required. This past spring, the FCC announced a sweeping ban on new foreign-made routers — like the kind you use to get online with your ISP and connect all your devices to Wi-Fi. This was all done in the name of national security, but just how real of a threat do routers pose? The discovery of a new security vulnerability in some Chinese-made routers may have you looking at the FCC’s action in a slightly more sympathetic light. Jacob Baines at VulnCheck shares his analysis of routers made by Zbtlink, sold under both that and Wiflyer branding. While neither are huge names in the router space, they’re still sold through US retailers like Amazon , and have been around for years — so, plenty of time for these devices to make some inroads on the market.

summary: Leaked images offer an early look at Samsung’s upcoming mid-tier flagship in three colors.
body: TL;DR The Samsung Galaxy S26 FE has just appeared in a series of images, revealing three color options. Among the major visual differences from the Galaxy S25 FE is the rear camera setup, which now resembles that of the Galaxy S26. Samsung hasn’t set a date for the phone’s launch, but a company executive recently confirmed it’s on the way. Following the launch of Samsung’s latest range of foldables, the focus now shifts to the company’s next smartphone, the Galaxy S26 FE. We’re now being treated to a series of official-looking images detailing the Galaxy S26 FE, giving us our best look yet of the smartphone. The blue model we’re seeing here doesn’t look too dissimilar to the Galaxy S25 FE in the Navy colorway (as you can see up top).

title: Google Search patches bug that broke time filters
summary: The widespread bug that ignored selected date ranges has now been resolved.
body: TL;DR Google has fixed the Search time filter bug that ignored selected date ranges. A Google Search VP confirmed the fix shipped earlier this week. If time filters are still broken, Google is asking users to report it. Good news for anyone who spent the past few days struggling to find recent news or software updates: Google has finally fixed its broken Search time filter feature. We recently reported that Google Search’s time filters — such as “Past 24 hours,” “Past month,” or custom date ranges — had stopped working globally. Instead of isolating results to your chosen timeframe, Search returned a random mix of old and new content, forcing users to rely on manual search operators as a workaround.

title: AYANEO’s new Game Boy Advance clone is more affordable than expected
summary: The handheld starts at just $89.
body: TL;DR AYANEO’s Game Boy Advance-inspired KONKR Pocket Advance is available to preorder now, starting at $89. The handheld is powered by MediaTek’s Helio G90T, the same chip found in the AYANEO Pocket Air Mini. The Pocket Advance boasts a 3.5-inch 960×640 display, a 4,000mAh battery, Android 12, active cooling, and more. If you’ve been waiting for AYANEO’s latest Android handheld to finally arrive, now’s the time to get your wallet ready. Oh, and the good news is that your wallet won’t be getting much lighter than previously expected! AYANEO’s Game Boy Advance (GBA) clone, which was first teased early in July , is finally available to pre-order. It’s called the KONKR Pocket Advance , and we finally have in-depth information about it.

title: Google Wallet now lets kids tap to pay without giving up parental control
summary: Your child gets tap to pay, but not a free pass to overspend.
body: TL;DR Google Wallet now supports supervised balances for kids and teens under 18 in the US, giving them a way to make digital payments with parental oversight. Parents can set daily spending limits, view transaction history, receive Family Link purchase alerts, and remotely lock the Wallet if a device is lost. Kids can tap to pay using their Android phone or Wear OS smartwatch anywhere Google Pay is accepted. Giving kids money has always involved a bit of trust. Maybe it’s cash for a weekend outing, a card for an emergency, or money to grab something while they’re out with friends. The problem is that cash is easy to lose, cards can go missing, and it’s not always obvious where the money ended up. That’s exactly the problem Google Wallet is now trying to solve. The company is rolling out supervised Google Wallet balances for children and teenagers under 18 in the US. Instead of handing your child a debit card and simply hoping they spend responsibly, you’ll be able to decide how much money they have access to while still keeping an eye on where it’s going. It’s a much more practical way to let kids start managing their own money without throwing them in at the deep end.

title: Mysterious new Garmin smartwatch spotted in FCC filings
summary: The unannounced device offers LTE and satellite connectivity.
body: Credit: Ryan Haines / Android Authority TL;DR A new Garmin smartwatch has been spotted in an FCC filing. The device carries the model number A05170 and has support for LTE and satellite connectivity. It also features 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi, Bluetooth Low Energy, ANT/ANT+, and NFC. Now that the Cirqa Smart Band is out, you may be wondering what else Garmin is working on. This will come as a surprise, but it turns out that the company’s next product will be a smartwatch. I know, I know, no one could’ve seen that coming. This smartwatch was recently spotted in a regulatory filing. The folks over at Gadgets and Wearables found the filing sitting in the FCC’s database. These documents don’t include the name of the device, but they do reveal that the model number is A05170. Additionally, Garmin describes the hardware as a portable digital transceiver, but the SAR evaluation report calls it a wrist-worn device.

title: Survey confirms your Fold 8 preference aligns with Samsung pre-orders
summary: We need more square phones.
body: Samsung’s latest foldable lineup is a departure from what the company’s been doing up to now. Rather than the usual two foldables — a Flip and a Fold — Samsung’s released three, including two book-style Z Fold phones in different aspect ratios. People have seemed excited about the new, wider form factor (the marginally less premium of the two) since before the phones were released , and now a survey Android Authority ‘s been running has confirmed that vibe. In a poll we’ve been running since late July, we asked readers which of the two Z Fold 8 phones they’d be more likely to buy. There were four options: the wide Z Fold 8; the narrow, higher-end Z Fold 8 Ultra; a response for people who hadn’t decided yet; and one for folks who just aren’t interested. After more than 1,000 responses, the wide Z Fold 8 ran away with it, nabbing nearly 60% of all votes.

title: Did the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra’s crease get worse after a couple of weeks?
summary: A tipster says the Z Fold 8 Ultra's crease has gotten worse over time. But has it?
body: Credit: Shimul Sood / Android Authority TL;DR A tipster has posted an image comparing the creases on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra and OPPO Find N6. The tipster claimed that the Z Fold 8 Ultra’s crease got worse after less than two weeks of use. We can also confirm that the Ultra phone’s crease is more pronounced, but that it still feels the same. Samsung’s new foldable phones generally have less prominent creases than their predecessors, bringing us a little closer to a zero-crease future. However, at least one Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra owner reports that the crease has become more visible after mere days. Tipster @sondesix posted a picture comparing the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra to the OPPO Find N6 (h/t: PhoneArena ). The user later remarked that the Z Fold 8 Ultra’s crease became more prominent after just under two weeks of usage. The image does suggest that the Samsung phone has a more noticeable crinkle.

title: I’m glad Google is making the Pixel Tag, but I absolutely won’t buy one
summary: The Pixel Tag won't tempt split Apple and Google households like mine.
body: Apple is excellent at building product ecosystems — it’s ready to sell you almost everything you need for your iPhone, from AirPods to AirTags. Comparatively, Google has been slower to expand its Pixel hardware lineup. There are still glaring holes in the Pixel portfolio, including over-ear headphones and Bluetooth trackers. However, Google might be filling the latter hole with the Pixel Tag, a Bluetooth tracker built for the Google Find Hub network . It’ll be the perfect Android alternative to the AirTag and Apple’s Find My network… or will it?

title: Nothing is literally doubling down on its smartphone ambitions, contrary to previous report
summary: Nothing suggests it will launch up to six phones in 2027, doubling the total number of phones it released this year.

Nothing seems to have more products planned for launch this quarter, though Evangelidis didn’t specify if they were phones or other devices. Nothing has largely succeeded in capturing the tech industry’s imagination despite being a relatively new entrant. Following the Phone 1, the company has released multiple flagships, including the Phone 4a Pro earlier this year . We’re now getting an early glimpse of the company’s ambitious plans for 2027, even as the tech world struggles with the RAM crisis. In an interview with Times Now Tech , Nothing co-founder Akis Evangelidis revealed the company plans to launch twice as many phones in 2027 as it did this year. If our math is accurate, this could potentially mean the release of up to six Nothing devices next year. For reference, Nothing has released three smartphones in 2026, including the vanilla Phone 4a, the Phone 4a Pro, and the Phone 4b . “We’ll share more details closer to launch, but the idea is …

summary: Aurzen's budget Roku TV projector comes with a preorder deal that's too hard to ignore.

This one costs less than $100, and while we’re awaiting details, Aurzen is already teasing a slight variation to the design compared to the previous model. Aurzen recently opened the floor for preorders for its upcoming EAZZE E1R projector with Roku ahead of the September 1 launch. The company is letting interested folks reserve theirs by paying just $1. In exchange, these early backers will get a $30 discount voucher that they can redeem on both Aurzen’s website and Amazon.

title: Chrome on Android is falling behind — here are 5 features it needs now
summary: Google needs to do better.
body: Credit: Mishaal Rahman / Android Authority Chrome on Android hasn’t kept up. That’s not a hot take — it’s just where things stand. And this is something you only realize once you step out and try other browsers like Firefox, Brave, Edge, and Samsung Internet. Extensions, proper privacy controls, customization, and background playback — competing browsers have been checking these boxes for years. The list of things Chrome still hasn’t gotten around to is longer than it should be, and it’s high time Google closed the gap.

title: One year of updates couldn’t save the Pixel 10’s GPU — and now the Pixel 11 is at risk
summary: What's the state of play with Android 17 on the Pixel 10?
body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority The Pixel 10 series may be Google’s best phones yet, but gamers got the short end of the stick. The Tensor G5 marked Google’s switch away from Arm’s Mali GPUs in favor of Imagination Technologies’ PowerVR architecture — specifically the mid-range, already aging DXT-48-1536. With the Pixel 11 launch approaching, one question keeps nagging at me: will history repeat itself? Rumors suggest the Tensor G6 will use another modest PowerVR GPU, the CXTP-48-1536. If Google’s recent trajectory is anything to go by, the Pixel 11 could fall even further behind rival flagship GPUs.

title: Samsung confirms minor setback for Galaxy S26 One UI 9 beta
summary: Samsung has delayed One UI 9 beta 5 for the S26 series until next week for "final reviews and quality improvements."
body: Credit: Paul Jones / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung has pushed the fifth One UI 9 beta 5 update for the Galaxy S26 series to next week. The delay is due to final reviews and quality improvements to enhance system stability and fix bugs before a stable release. The over-the-air update will roll out to enrolled Galaxy S26, S26 Plus, and S26 Ultra devices in the US, UK, India, Germany, Poland, and South Korea when it goes live next week. Samsung has confirmed a short delay for the fifth beta build of One UI 9 for the Galaxy S26 series, pushing its expected release into next week. Galaxy S26 owners participating in the preview program will have to hold on a bit longer, following the rollout of the One UI 9 beta 4 update last month. According to an official announcement post on the Samsung Community forum (via Tarun Vats on X ), the development team is taking additional time for “final reviews and quality improvements” before rolling out the fifth iteration. Samsung apologized to community members for the slight delay, citing the need to deliver a more stable, polished software experience to testers.

title: Galaxy S26 FE appears at FCC with an unexpected Qualcomm twist

The filing also mentions both Qualcomm and Samsung Exynos wireless technologies. A closer look suggests that the phone will have a Samsung modem and chipset, as well as a Qualcomm local networking chip. Samsung has just launched its new foldable phones , but we’re already looking forward to the Galaxy S26 FE ‘s imminent arrival. The phone is expected to launch in the coming weeks, and a regulatory filing has revealed a few details. The Galaxy S26 FE passed through the FCC’s database, and the filing reveals a few notable features. For one, the listing hints at both Qualcomm and Samsung Exynos silicon in the same model. Wait, what?

title: Google may finally fix a major frustration with Android’s Photo Picker
summary: Code in Android 17 QPR 2 Beta 2 reveals plans for a built-in media editor, which could save users from tedious app switching.
body: Credit: Mishaal Rahman / Android Authority TL;DR Google is laying the groundwork to add a built-in media editor directly to the Android Photo Picker. Code in Android 17 QPR2 Beta 2 reveals an “EditFeature” class designed as a pop-up dialog for quick edits like cropping and marking. Because the Photo Picker updates via Google Play System Updates, this feature can roll out independently of a full OS update. Android’s Photo Picker is a system component that provides third-party apps with a browsable interface for accessing media library content. It’s a massive leap forward for user privacy, as it allows users to share specific photos and videos with third-party apps without giving them access to their full media library. For app developers, it saves them the effort of building this interface themselves. Google has refocused its efforts on improving the Android Photo Picker, as we’ve spotted features like a camera shortcut in the works. You can look forward to another new feature coming soon: a media editor. You’re reading an Authority Insights story. Scores of Pixel users are now complaining of touch-related issues since upgrading to Android 17. Seemingly unrelated to the previously reported bug that led to temporarily unresponsive Pixel touchscreens , the new issue only seems to affect users inside games or certain other apps. According to a few reports on Reddit and Google Community forums , the issue appears especially when an app occupies the screen entirely, such as when playing a video on YouTube. Giv…

title: These Game Boy-like Android handhelds are coming soon at a fantastic price
summary: You don't have to spend a ton of cash to get a capable vertical Android handheld.

title: This robot vacuum cleaner comes with dual RGB cameras and a self-cleaning mop
summary: Finally, a robot vacuum cleaner that won't wake up your sleeping baby.
body: TL;DR Narwal has launched the new Narwal Freo 20 robot vacuum cleaner. It comes with a self-cleaning mop and dual RGB cameras. It offers interactive video monitoring and can identify baby toys and cribs to automatically switch to a low-noise cleaning mode. Narwal is today launching a brand-new robot vacuum cleaner — the Narwal Freo 20 — and it comes with a ton of features, including the first-ever self-cleaning mopping system in the Freo series. The Freo 20 is the first robot vacuum outside the Narwal Flow series to feature Narwal’s “FlowWash” mopping system. It uses 16 nozzles to spray hot water directly onto the mop to keep it clean while it mops your house. The company claims that this ensures better cleaning without leaving water streaks on the floor.

title: Google Home kicks off August with big app updates and a smarter Gemini for Home
summary: Google Home's first August update is packed with useful new features.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Google has added an interactive AI Storytime feature to Gemini for Home that lets families create and modify stories using voice commands. The update also improves alarms, timers, and other everyday features while fixing several bugs. The Google Home app now supports more smart camera brands and includes several new camera viewing and recording improvements. Google has announced a fresh batch of updates for Gemini for Home (Early access) and the Google Home app. The latest August 5 update adds a fun new AI-powered Storytime feature to Gemini for Home and promises to make everyday smart home controls more reliable in the app.

title: Galaxy Z8 preorders are surging, and one model is leading the charge
summary: Samsung’s foldable gamble appears to be paying off big time.
body: TL;DR Samsung says global preorders for the Galaxy Z8 series increased by more than 30% over the previous generation. The Galaxy Z8 lineup is on pace to set a new US preorder record for Samsung foldables. The regular Galaxy Z Fold 8 accounts for nearly half of US Z8 preorders across carriers and retailers. Foldable phones have often been described as a niche market, always hovering somewhere between exciting technology and expensive curiosity. However, the latest generation of Samsung foldables appears to be finding a bigger audience. Samsung says global preorders for the Galaxy Z8 series are up more than 30% over last year’s lineup, while the phones are also on pace to set a new Galaxy Z preorder record in the US. The company says combined US preorders for the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Fold 8 Ultra are running 30% ahead of its previous record-holding Fold generation after the first 12 days. That follows the Z8 series setting an all-time preorder record for Samsung foldables in South Korea , so the enthusiasm clearly isn’t confined to one particularly foldable-friendly market.

title: Your Gemini for Home timers and alarms are getting smarter and more reliable
summary: The update also fixes the annoying Google Speaker light ring bug.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Gemini now lets you co-create stories on the fly, interrupt the narrative mid-scene, and remix classic tales. Google has made timers and alarms smarter and more accurate. Turning off a device now plays a soft, descending tone that matches the action. Two weeks ago, Google rolled out a Home update that allows Gemini to track conversations for longer . Fast forward to today, another Gemini for Home update is rolling out. Along with that, we’re getting smarter timers and alarms, as well as a few bug fixes. Story time with Gemini Starting with the latest change to Gemini, Google says on its support page that it is making story time interactive. Specifically, you’ll now be able to co-create stories on the fly, interrupt the narrative mid-scene, and remix classic tales. For example, you could tell Gemini to create a story about your kids traveling to Mars. Midway through, you could tell the AI to jump to the part where they reach the red planet. Or if you tell Gemini to recite the story of the three little pigs, you could ask to replace the big bad wolf with a T-Rex.

title: TCL’s super-thin bezels make its next mid-tier phones look like flagships
summary: TCL is cooking up two mid-range phones with flagship-thin bezels.
body: Credit: Roland Quandt TL;DR A leak has revealed renders of two new TCL phones. The P80 Pro will reportedly come with a MediaTek 7400 Elite chip, 6.83-inch OLED display, and 5,800mAh battery. The base model offers a 7300 Elite chip, 5,000mAh battery, and 8GB of RAM/128GB of storage. TCL recently launched the NXTPAPER version of the Tab A1 Plus . While the tablet is currently available for purchase, you’ll have to wait for the company’s next products. TCL has two new handsets on the way, and a leak provides not only our first look, but also the first details. In one of his latest social posts, Roland Quandt revealed that TCL is working on the P80 and P80 Pro. According to Quandt, the tan colored device is the base model, while the gray device is the Pro version. Both phones are fairly reminiscent of the NXTPAPER 70 Pro , minus two big differences. One of those differences is that these screens don’t have a matte finish, and the other is the flagship-like thin bezels.
